A 72-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of a new right-sided headache and two brief episodes of vision loss in the right eye. For 1 month, she has had fatigue, aching in both shoulders, and pain in her jaw while chewing. Examination shows tenderness over the right temporal artery. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 96 mm/h. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate next step in management?
A. Begin high-dose glucocorticoid therapy
B. Obtain a temporal artery biopsy before initiating treatment
C. Prescribe sumatriptan as needed
D. Start low-dose aspirin as the only therapy
query:
A 72-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of a new right-sided headache and two brief episodes of vision loss in the right eye. For 1 month, she has had fatigue, aching in both shoulders, and pain in her jaw while chewing. Examination shows tenderness over the right temporal artery. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 96 mm/h. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate next step in management?
A. Begin high-dose glucocorticoid therapy
B. Obtain a temporal artery biopsy before initiating treatment
C. Prescribe sumatriptan as needed
D. Start low-dose aspirin as the only therapy
Choose the correct option.
options: B. Obtain a temporal artery biopsy before initiating treatment
D. Start low-dose aspirin as the only therapy
solution: The new headache, jaw claudication, polymyalgia rheumatica symptoms, markedly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, temporal artery tenderness, and transient monocular vision loss indicate giant cell arteritis with threatened permanent visual loss. High-dose glucocorticoids must be started immediately; diagnostic biopsy should not delay treatment because arterial inflammation can rapidly cause irreversible blindness.
explanation: Suspected giant cell arteritis with visual symptoms requires immediate high-dose glucocorticoids. Temporal artery biopsy can confirm the diagnosis after therapy has begun.

Laboratory studies show a serum glucose concentration of 510 mg/dL, arterial pH of 7.12, bicarbonate concentration of 9 mEq/L, and serum potassium concentration of 5.6 mEq/L. Which of the following best describes this patient's potassium balance before treatment?
A. Increased total-body potassium due to reduced renal excretion
B. Normal total-body potassium with increased intracellular stores
C. Decreased total-body potassium despite the elevated serum concentration
D. Decreased total-body potassium caused primarily by insulin administration
query:
A 19-year-old man with type 1 diabetes mellitus is brought to the emergency department because of vomiting and progressive lethargy. His respirations are deep and rapid. Laboratory studies show a serum glucose concentration of 510 mg/dL, arterial pH of 7.12, bicarbonate concentration of 9 mEq/L, and serum potassium concentration of 5.6 mEq/L. Which of the following best describes this patient's potassium balance before treatment?
A. Increased total-body potassium due to reduced renal excretion
B. Normal total-body potassium with increased intracellular stores
C. Decreased total-body potassium despite the elevated serum concentration
D. Decreased total-body potassium caused primarily by insulin administration
Choose the correct option.
options: A. Increased total-body potassium due to reduced renal excretion
B. Normal total-body potassium with increased intracellular stores
C. Decreased total-body potassium despite the elevated serum concentration
D. Decreased total-body potassium caused primarily by insulin administration
solution: This patient has diabetic ketoacidosis. Insulin deficiency and hyperosmolality shift potassium from the intracellular space into serum, so the measured serum potassium can be high. At the same time, osmotic diuresis, vomiting, and urinary ketoanion losses produce a substantial net loss of potassium from the body. Therefore, total-body potassium is depleted even before insulin is given.
explanation: In diabetic ketoacidosis, extracellular potassium may be elevated by transcellular shifts, but total-body potassium is decreased because of urinary and gastrointestinal losses.
answer: C. Decreased total-body potassium despite the elevated serum concentration

query:

explanation: Minimal change disease is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children and is characterized ultrastructurally by podocyte foot-process effacement.
answer: C. Diffuse effacement of podocyte foot processes on electron microscopy

Examination shows decreased vibration sense in both legs. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin of 9.4 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume of 113 fL. A peripheral smear shows macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils. Which of the following metabolites is most likely increased in this patient?
A. Homogentisic acid only
B. Methylmalonic acid and homocysteine
C. Orotic acid and ammonia
D. Uric acid and xanthine
query:
A 58-year-old man comes to the physician because of progressive fatigue and numbness in his feet. He underwent total gastrectomy 4 years ago for gastric cancer. Examination shows decreased vibration sense in both legs. Laboratory studies show hemoglobin of 9.4 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume of 113 fL. A peripheral smear shows macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils. Which of the following metabolites is most likely increased in this patient?
A. Homogentisic acid only
B. Methylmalonic acid and homocysteine
C. Orotic acid and ammonia
D. Uric acid and xanthine
Choose the correct option.
solution: Total gastrectomy eliminates intrinsic-factor production, eventually causing vitamin B12 deficiency after hepatic stores are depleted. Macrocytic megaloblastic anemia plus neurologic deficits supports this diagnosis. Vitamin B12 is required for both methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and methionine synthase, so deficiency increases both methylmalonic acid and homocysteine.
explanation: Vitamin B12 deficiency after gastrectomy causes megaloblastic anemia and neurologic findings, with elevations of both methylmalonic acid and homocysteine.

A. 5-alpha-reductase
B. 11-beta-hydroxylase
C. 17-alpha-hydroxylase
D. 21-hydroxylase
query:
A 10-day-old girl is brought to the emergency department because of poor feeding and repeated vomiting. She has lost 12% of her birth weight. Examination shows dehydration and clitoromegaly. Laboratory studies show sodium of 124 mEq/L, potassium of 6.4 mEq/L, glucose of 52 mg/dL, and low serum cortisol. Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is the most likely cause?
A. 5-alpha-reductase
B. 11-beta-hydroxylase
C. 17-alpha-hydroxylase
D. 21-hydroxylase
Choose the correct option.
solution: This newborn has a salt-wasting adrenal crisis with virilization, the classic presentation of severe 21-hydroxylase deficiency. Impaired cortisol and aldosterone synthesis causes hypoglycemia, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and volume depletion. Steroid precursors are diverted toward androgen production, causing virilization of an affected 46,XX infant.
explanation: 21-hydroxylase deficiency decreases cortisol and aldosterone while increasing adrenal androgens, producing salt wasting and virilization.
